page: Vultr vx1-m-4c-32gb is a memory-optimized server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a bundled 1 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10% tier. Geekbench text processing also ranks in the top tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance is more limited, with Geekbench multi-core and clang software compilation benchmarks falling into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 440.83 GB/sec for cached reads and 69.51 GB/sec for uncached reads.

Given the high memory capacity relative to the 4 vCPUs, this server is well-suited for memory-intensive, single-threaded, or memory-cached workloads such as Redis deployments, which achieve an average of 8.06 million operations per second. It is also appropriate for database operations and text processing. The primary tradeoff is the small 1 GB local NVMe SSD storage, which necessitates external storage for data-heavy applications, and the weaker multi-threaded performance which makes it less suitable for heavy parallel compilation or large-scale LLM inference.
